status: PROPOSAL ONLY -- NOT EXECUTED, NOT INSTALLED. No crontab entry has been added or modified as part of producing this document. Explicit separate human authorization is required before installation.
required_env_for_command_above: HOT_COLD_ROLLOVER_CONFIRM=YES-RETIRE-PRODUCTION-HOT-ROWS must be set in the cron environment (or exported in the shell wrapper invoking the command) -- without it, the command above runs safely in COPY_VERIFY_ONLY_UNCONFIRMED mode and deletes nothing, per the double-gate default-safe design.

proposed_cadence.reasoning: Matches the P5C contract sketch's proposal (different hour from the existing 03:00 P2.2 cleanup job to avoid overlap). Verified against the CURRENT real crontab (Part 1/25 census): */5 helius monitor, 0 */4 graph analyzers, 0 * migration coverage audit (hourly, so it DOES run at 04:00 too -- but it is a short read-mostly audit job against a different concern, not a HOT write-lock-heavy job, so co-occurrence at the top of the hour is judged low-risk; if first-run observation shows contention, shifting to 04:07 avoids the hourly job's exact top-of-hour firing), and 0 3 storage_lifecycle_runner (P2.2, narrow temp-file cleanup, different scope entirely). 04:00 remains clear of the 0-3 and 0-*/4 jobs' exact minute, and quiet-traffic-period reasoning from P5C's growth observations (ingestion is not obviously day/night patterned in the short sample available, so 04:00 is chosen primarily for cron-slot cleanliness, not a proven traffic trough).

batch_size.evidence: docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5d_lock_safety.json batch_size_qualification -- measured max HOT retirement transaction duration of 4.62ms at batch_size=500 against a 5000-row fixture, versus 5.32ms at 100 and 7.09ms at 5000. 500 chosen for flatter per-batch lock hold time and a sensible number of batches (~19-20) against the real measured backlog of 9,590 rows.

max_rows_per_run_reasoning: The real measured net-new-eligible backlog (9,590 rows, Part 18) is well under this ceiling, so a single scheduled run is expected to fully clear the current backlog plus several days of newly-aged-out rows without needing multiple scheduled invocations. The ceiling exists as a safety bound against an unexpectedly large backlog (e.g. after an extended period of automation being off), not as a routine constraint.
max_wall_time: Not separately enforced by a wall-clock cutoff in this implementation -- bounded instead by max_rows_per_run (50,000 rows at ~500/batch = 100 batches; fixture measurements show ~0.03-0.05s of pipeline overhead per batch excluding I/O against a real 13GB file, so a full 50,000-row run is expected to complete in well under a minute of runner-side compute; real production I/O time against the live 13GB file was not benchmarked in this qualification pass and should be observed on the first real activated run).

lock_policy.lease_path: database/hot_cold_rollover.lease (a NEW lease file, separate from database/storage_lifecycle.lock used by the existing P2.2 job -- the two jobs never contend with each other's lease, only (potentially) with SQLite's own file-level locking on the HOT db during the P5D job's brief retirement transactions, which is bounded and measured above)
lock_policy.behavior_on_contention: non-blocking -- a second concurrent invocation (e.g. a manually triggered run overlapping the scheduled one) receives CleanupLeaseHeldError immediately and exits cleanly with zero rows touched, exactly like the existing P2.2 runner's pattern.

busy_policy.mechanism: PRAGMA busy_timeout=2000 (2s) on the HOT retirement write connection; on sqlite3.OperationalError (locked/busy) the CURRENT batch aborts (abort_reason='HOT_RETIREMENT_BUSY: ...'), already-copied+verified COLD data for that batch is retained, and the run stops (does not retry in a loop, does not skip ahead).

disk_thresholds.behavior: STOP: run aborts before touching anything, reports DISK_GUARD_STOP. CAUTION: currently proceeds (the design's 'stop-unless-proven-safe' framing is implemented as a reported state; the qualification build proceeds through CAUTION rather than hard-stopping, since COLD writes for a 500-row batch are on the order of tens of KB, far below a level that would meaningfully worsen a 25 GiB-free situation) -- flagged for tightening (hard-stop at CAUTION too) if a future review judges the current behavior too permissive.

audit_log_location.run_ledger: docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5d_execution_ledger.jsonl (append-only JSON lines via src.ops.storage_audit_ledger.append_entry, same LedgerEntry shape already used by the P2.2 job)
audit_log_location.cron_stdout_stderr: logs/hot_cold_rollover.log (proposed, matching the existing logs/storage_lifecycle.log and logs/graph_analyzers.log convention)

stop_conditions: Disk guard STOP state (<=20 GiB free) -- abort before any work.
Lease already held by a concurrent invocation -- abort immediately, zero rows touched.

COLD verification mismatch for any batch -- abort the WHOLE run, leave HOT untouched, leave the mismatched COLD segment in place for human investigation (NOT auto-discarded, matching the P5C contract sketch's quarantine intent -- note: this qualification build does not yet implement the .verify_failed rename step from the P5C sketch; it aborts and logs but does not rename the segment file. Flagged as a small gap to close before activation if segment quarantine renaming is judged necessary; the run-halting fail-closed behavior itself is fully implemented and tested).
SQLITE_BUSY / database locked on the HOT retirement transaction -- abort the current batch, preserve already-verified COLD data, stop the run.
max_rows_per_run ceiling reached -- clean stop, resumable next scheduled run via the persisted checkpoint.
first_run_observation_procedure: 1. Run manually ONCE with --dry-run first (zero writes) and review the JSON report: rows_scanned, pinned_excluded, copied ('would copy') counts should roughly match the Part 18 census (approximately 9,590 net-new eligible, though the exact figure will have drifted by the time of activation).

2. Run manually ONCE with --copy-verify-only (writes COLD, never retires HOT) against production. Confirm the resulting segment(s) under database/_p5a_migration_build/cold_segments/ via ColdSegmentRegistry, confirm row counts match the dry-run report, confirm a spot-check of several archived signatures is readable identically before/after via UnifiedTransferReader.

3. Only after step 2's segments are human-reviewed and closed (close_segment()), run the FIRST real-retire pass manually (not yet via cron) with both the CLI flag and the env var set, on a small --max-rows (e.g. 2000) to observe real production HOT retirement transaction timing and lease behavior under live traffic.

4. Confirm the 3 writer services show no new lock-error log entries during and immediately after the manual real-retire pass (grep watchtower_listener/creator_funding_worker/watchtower_api logs for 'database is locked'/'database is busy' in a window around the run).

5. Only after steps 1-4 all pass cleanly does installing the cron entry become appropriate -- and that installation itself requires separate explicit human authorization per this milestone's boundary, not automatic follow-on from a clean qualification.
rollback_disable_procedure: To disable: remove the cron entry (once installed) -- the runner has no other persistent state that needs deactivating. No supervisord program is proposed, so there is nothing to stop/restart.

To pause without removing: the runner's own default-safe behavior means simply NOT setting HOT_COLD_ROLLOVER_CONFIRM in the cron environment reverts it to COPY_VERIFY_ONLY_UNCONFIRMED mode automatically -- COLD segments continue accumulating (harmless, append-only) but HOT retirement stops immediately, with zero code change required.

If a bad COLD segment is ever published: it can be excluded from ColdSegmentRegistry by moving it out of the cold_root directory (the registry only globs *.sqlite files present at build() time); this does not affect HOT (already-retired rows would need restoration from the rollback DB in the worst case, which is why database/flex_complete_database.db.p5b_rollback_quarantine remains retained per the existing P5B/P5C retention policy, unaffected by this milestone).
This runner never modifies the existing P2.2 storage_lifecycle_runner.py or its cron entry, so disabling P5D has zero effect on that job.
next_action: Activation (installing the cron entry) requires separate explicit human authorization -- this contract is a qualified proposal, not a decision.
